general.title_original: ‘No-money’ Indian YouTuber sparks fury over attempt to sleep at Thai temple
general.summary_original:
UDON THANI – An Indian travel YouTuber has drawn online criticism after posting a video about being asked to leave a temple in Udon Thani, where he said he had sought shelter because he had no money.

The YouTuber, identified as Banshi, who has around 17,300 subscribers, titled the video “Thailand Good Police Say Get Out of The Temple Now || First Bad Experience In Thailand Temple”.

In the video, Banshi said he had been travelling in Thailand without money and had relied on asking people for help and food. Local police and temple committee members asked him to pack his belongings and leave, explaining that the temple was not a place for outsiders to stay overnight.

According to the account in the video, officers and temple representatives expressed concern for his safety and suggested that he stay at a budget hotel costing around 400 baht per night. They also offered to help him get there, but he declined, saying he wanted to travel on an extremely tight budget.

Banshi later moved his belongings to a petrol station to spend the night. Police also advised him on safety and how to continue his journey appropriately.

The video prompted a wave of criticism, with commenters questioning his decision to travel without sufficient funds and expecting free accommodation.

One commenter said travellers should respect local communities and avoid sleeping in public places without permission, adding that people who could not afford accommodation should reconsider their travel plans.

Another praised the officers for their handling of the situation, saying they had treated Banshi politely and offered a reasonable accommodation option. The commenter also urged him to respect local rules and understand that temples are places of worship, not free campsites.

Some criticism also came from people identifying themselves as Indian or members of the Indian community in Thailand. They said his conduct could reinforce negative stereotypes about Indian tourists and urged him to travel responsibly.

The online reaction focused largely on expectations of free accommodation and the responsibility of visitors to consider local rules and safety concerns.

general.title_original: Bangkok bans gatherings disrupting IMF-World Bank meetings at 24 venues
general.summary_original:
BANGKOK – Thailand has banned public gatherings that obstruct access or disrupt operations at 24 venues hosting events and delegates during the 2026 annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Group.

The announcement was published in the Royal Gazette on 11 October, ahead of the meetings scheduled for 12-18 October at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Centre (QSNCC) in Bangkok.

The restrictions cover the convention centre, One Bangkok Forum, where official receptions will be held, and 22 hotels accommodating delegates and dignitaries.

The Metropolitan Police Bureau said the measures prohibit gatherings that block entrances and exits or interfere with the operation of, or access to, the designated venues.

The restrictions took effect on 10 October and will remain in force until 20 October.

Police urged the public and all sectors to cooperate in welcoming delegates from around the world.

Anyone wishing to report suspicious activity or seek traffic information can contact the emergency hotline at 191 or the Traffic Control and Command Centre at 1197, both available around the clock.

แหล่งข่าวระบุว่า การหารือครั้งนี้สะท้อนถึงความกังวลที่เพ…

general.summary:
ทักษิณ ยื่น พ.ร.บ.สันติสุข ขอพ้นผิด คดีการเมือง-ล้างมลทินคดีชินคอร์ป อ้างพิษรัฐประหาร49
ภายหลัง คณะกรรมการสร้างเสริมสังคมสันติสุข ประชุมนัดแรก กลั่นกรองนิรโทษกรรมคดีการเมือง หวังยุติความขัดแย้ง 20 ปี ตามกฎหมายว่าด้วยการนิรโทษกรรมคดีการเมือง มีขึ้นในวันนี้ 21 กันยายน)ที่ทำเนียบรัฐบาล โดยมี นายปกรณ์ นิลประพันธ์ รองนายกรัฐมนตรี เป็นประธานคณะกรรมการ และมีการตั้งคณะอนุกรรมการฯ ขึ้นมา 2 ชุด ชุดแรกจะเป็…

general.title: เมื่อ AI เปลี่ยนโลกสื่อ… ทรูเปิดบ้านรับ คณะผู้เข้าอบรมหลักสูตรบยสส. รุ่นที่ 5

general.title: JAS-MONOMAX-ไปรษณีย์ไทย ผนึกเปิดแคมเปญ เชียร์พรีเมียร์ลีก ลุ้นโชค ขยายฐานแฟนทั่วประเทศ

อย่างไรก็ตาม คะแนนดังกล่…

general.title: เฮียหน่อย อีสานนครศิลป์ เคลียร์ดราม่า ประกาศขายวงหมอลำ 50 ล้าน ลั่นเปลี่ยนเพื่อให้โอกาสคนรุ่นใหม่
general.summary:
เฮียหน่อย อีสานนครศิลป์ เคลียร์ดราม่า ประกาศขายวงหมอลำ 50 ล้าน ลั่นเปลี่ยนเพื่อให้โอกาสคนรุ่นใหม่

general.title: พิชญ์ พงษ์สวัสดิ์ | คิดใหม่เรื่องน้ำท่วมเมือง
general.summary:

BANGKOK — 12 October 2026, Social media users have expressed outrage after concertgoers reported that someone defecated in the standing area during The Weeknd’s concert at Rajamangala National Stadium.

Following the major concert on Sunday night, several attendees took to X (formerly Twitter) to complain about what they described as disgusting behavior in the standing zone.

Some posts also alleged that foreign concertgoers had been smoking cigarettes and cannabis inside the venue, adding to complaints about concert etiquette.

The reports sparked frustration among fans, who said the alleged incidents had marred their concert experience.

The claims circulated widely on social media, although the accounts and identities of those allegedly involved were not independently verified.

general.title_original: American man, 69, killed in collision with ice delivery truck in Nakhon Phanom
general.summary_original:
NAKHON PHANOM – An American man aged 69 was killed after his motorcycle was struck from behind by an ice delivery truck on a bypass road in Nakhon Phanom on Monday, police said.

Police from Muang Nakhon Phanom station were alerted to the accident on the Nakhon Phanom-Tha Uthen bypass road, heading into the city, on 12 October.

The victim, identified as Daniel, was found dead beneath the truck. His motorcycle, a Honda, was found overturned nearby, with its rear section crushed and the rear wheel bent out of shape.

The truck, a white Toyota vehicle fitted with an enclosed cargo compartment, had also struck a streetlight pole. Its driver, Lamphorn Chanjumpum, 47, a resident of the area, remained at the scene to give a statement.

A preliminary investigation found that the truck was delivering ice when it collided with the motorcycle, which had reportedly just left Big C Nakhon Phanom shopping centre. The victim was believed to have been heading home to Chom Khong village in the city.

Police suspect the truck was travelling at high speed and could not stop in time before hitting the motorcycle from behind. The impact reportedly threw the motorcycle off balance, while the truck continued into a streetlight pole. The victim became trapped beneath the vehicle and died at the scene.

Police are reviewing CCTV footage from the surrounding area and conducting further investigations to establish the exact cause of the accident. They will also notify the US Embassy because an American citizen died in the crash.

After the accident, a female Immigration Bureau police officer arrived at the scene and identified herself as the victim’s wife. She said they had lived together for several years, with her husband choosing to stay in Nakhon Phanom because he liked the local atmosphere.

She said he regularly rode his motorcycle to Big C to buy food, despite owning a car, and had been doing so before the fatal accident.

general.title: Livestream clash raises questions over tourist conduct, filming, and violence in Thailand
general.summary:
A confrontation between a Korean livestreamer and a tuk-tuk driver in Bangkok has divided viewers over a difficult question: where is the line between a tourist’s right to create content in public and another person’s wish not to appear in it?
The footage, recorded during a livestream by Kick creator TAEMIN1998, shows a heated argument after a tuk-tuk driver believed he was being filmed. The stre…
general.title_original: Livestream clash raises questions over tourist conduct, filming, and violence in Thailand
general.summary_original:
A confrontation between a Korean livestreamer and a tuk-tuk driver in Bangkok has divided viewers over a difficult question: where is the line between a tourist’s right to create content in public and another person’s wish not to appear in it?

The footage, recorded during a livestream by Kick creator TAEMIN1998, shows a heated argument after a tuk-tuk driver believed he was being filmed. The streamer says he is recording himself rather than the driver. The driver repeatedly tells him to stop filming and leave.

For reference, in Thailand filming in public is generally allowed without asking everyone’s permission, but that does not give streamers an unrestricted right to record or broadcast people. Privacy laws may apply, depending on how the footage is used.

In practice, filming becomes more sensitive when a person has clearly objected, when footage identifies them in a potentially damaging context, or when it is posted with misleading claims. Private venues may also set their own rules on recording.

The exchange then escalates. Something appears to hit or graze the streamer’s face, and a second man later enters the frame. The camera jolts as TAEMIN1998 appears to be struck again. He later says he was hit several times.

TAEMIN1998 is a Korean livestreamer whose content centres on travelling and interacting with people in public. His Thailand broadcasts were part of an early-October trip that also took him through Bangkok and Phuket.

Commenters on the Reddit forum where the footage was reposted disagreed over whether he should be regarded as a “nuisance streamer” — a label commonly used online for creators whose content is seen as disruptive or provocative.

One user, called him “very much a nuisance streamer.” Another, CreamSodaCassanova, disagreed, describing him as “not a nuisance streamer” but someone who could be unaware and “not street smart.” These are personal assessments, not independent findings of Khaosod English.

The footage nevertheless drew a broader debate over conduct. Reddit user 8forever argued that the streamer should have stepped back after the driver objected, writing: “You’re a guest. Read the room. Respect people’s privacy.” The commenter also said people should not treat “ordinary people as unwilling extras” in a livestream, while adding that violence was not the right response.

Other users addressed the violence from the driver, saying that even if the driver believed he was being filmed, that “really doesn’t make attacking someone acceptable.”

That is the uncomfortable centre of this video. It is reasonable to believe that TAEMIN1998 handled the encounter poorly, or should have lowered the camera and left earlier, while also believing that apparent violence was not an acceptable response.

Tourists have a responsibility to be respectful guests. Thailand’s reputation for warmth should never be read as an invitation to treat local people, workers or public spaces as props for a livestream. Recording strangers at close range, challenging people after they object, or allowing an audience to encourage confrontation can quickly turn a minor misunderstanding into something uglier.

At the same time, visitors should be able to expect disagreements to be settled without violence. A dispute over a phone camera, a fare or a misunderstanding shouldn’t devolve into conversations about nationality and stereotypes.

The clip is a useful reminder for both tourists and locals: respect is reciprocal. Put the camera down when a situation is becoming tense. Walk away when an argument is going nowhere. And do not answer perceived disrespect with violence.
